questions.title: The classic example of a fibrous joint
questions.question: Which of the following is considered a classic example of fibrous joints?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The knee is a synovial joint (a modified hinge), with a joint cavity and articular cartilage — a different structural class from a fibrous joint.
explanations.B: Correct. Joints are classified structurally into fibrous, cartilaginous and synovial types. Fibrous joints are united by dense fibrous tissue with no joint cavity and essentially no movement (a synarthrosis), and the sutures between the flat bones of the skull vault are the textbook example. This contrasts sharply with the knee, shoulder and hip, which are all freely mobile synovial joints.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The shoulder is a synovial ball-and-socket joint, the most mobile joint in the body — structurally the opposite of a fibrous joint.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The hip is also a synovial ball-and-socket joint (though more stable and less mobile than the shoulder), with a joint cavity and articular cartilage, not a fibrous union.

questions.learning_objective: Name the sutures of the skull as the classic fibrous-joint example, contrasted with synovial joints.
